note: The short walkthrough's voice copy: one line a shot, as said (docs/demo/walkthrough.md is the master). 'say' is what the voice reads when it differs from the caption.

lines.text: Xenoform turns a song into a music video where every beat is a transformation.
Drop in a song and pick a vibe: molten gold, neon noir, ink and paper, or None, the things just as they are.
Then say what it morphs through. A theme like racing brings fifteen things of its own.
Make listens to the song, plans the shots on its bars and beats, picks the objects, and renders a morph for every shot.
Every shot is one object turning into the next, cut to the song's own bars.
Five ways to change, and the change can land right on the beat.
Effects ride the kick and the loudness.
Then edit it like a timeline. Colour, effects, order and cuts, shot by shot, re-cut from the cached morphs with no GPU.
Or morph your own film clips into each other.
A Draft in minutes, a Fast Final at 1080p, or the full LTX-2.3 Final.
lines.say: A Draft in minutes, a Fast Final at ten eighty p, or the full LTX 2.3 Final.

lines.text: How it's built: the song is split into stems and bars, the plan becomes ComfyUI graphs sent through the Comfy SDK, and LTX renders every morph on one 12 GB card. All open weights, all local.
lines.say: How it's built: the song is split into stems and bars, the plan becomes ComfyUI graphs sent through the Comfy SDK, and LTX renders every morph on one twelve gigabyte card. All open weights, all local.

lines.text: What's new: the edit comes from the music itself, every shot is generated, and you change it like an editor, not a prompt box. An MCP server lets any AI drive it.
